sectors.name: Social protection
sectors.tagline: Income supports, pensions and family payments
sectors.intro: Explore pensions, working-age income supports, children’s payments and disability and carer supports. This is the public cost of the programmes, not a calculation of your household’s entitlements.
sectors.note: The source separates “Pensions” (the non-contributory State Pension) from “Pension” (contributory and related payments). Both are retained below; they are different categories, not duplicates.

programmes.name: Working-age income supports
programmes.note: Explore the published income-support payment lines. An allocation describes scheme expenditure, not the amount any particular claimant receives. The source’s component coverage is incomplete.

programmes.name: Employment supports
programmes.note: Compare the published employment-support scheme lines within this programme. Funding totals alone do not show how many people entered or retained employment.

programmes.name: Children and family payments
programmes.note: Child Benefit, Working Family Payment and school meals appear here. The programme total is larger than the displayed component lines; the unexplained balance is shown rather than assigned to an invented scheme.
lines: Back To School Clothing and Footwear Allowance

programmes.name: Supplementary payments and agencies
programmes.original: Supplementary Payments, Agencies And Miscellaneous Services
programmes.note: This is a source-defined grouping of supplementary payments, agencies and miscellaneous services. Its displayed line items leave a balance that cannot be assigned to individual schemes from this source alone.
lines: Grant To the Citizens Information Board

programmes.name: Social Protection administration
programmes.note: The published administration lines distinguish operating costs within Social Protection. Do not treat the entire administration allocation as avoidable savings.

programmes.name: Non-contributory State Pension
programmes.note: The source calls this “Pensions” and identifies the State Pension (Non-contributory) as its single component. It is separate from the contributory pension group.

programmes.name: Illness, disability and carers
programmes.note: This group covers income-support programmes. It is distinct from disability services within the Children, Disability and Equality department. The displayed component list does not account for the whole programme total.

programmes.name: Pension auto-enrolment
programmes.note: Separate the State contribution from the allocation for the National Automatic Enrolment Retirement Savings Authority. These are public allocations, not the employee’s pension deduction.
lines: State Contributions To My Future Fund

programmes.name: Contributory and related pensions
programmes.note: This source group contains the State Pension (Contributory), bereaved partner contributory pension and the widow’s death benefit. It is not the non-contributory State Pension line.
lines: Widows', Widowers' / Surviving Civil Partners' (Death Benefit)

sectors.name: Health
sectors.tagline: Healthcare funding, capital services and HSE regions
sectors.intro: Follow the published health allocation through capital services, national programmes and the six HSE regional health areas. The figures describe funding categories; they are not hospital waiting-time or quality scores.
sectors.note: The six regional health area lines are accounting groupings, not six extra budgets to add to total health spending. They do not give a reliable county-by-county split or separate prices for every clinical service.

programmes.name: Department of Health administration
programmes.note: This is the Department of Health administration grouping. HSE corporate administration is a separate published programme; the two labels should not be substituted for each other.
lines: Operational Services, Supplies and Sundry Equipment

programmes.name: Health capital services
programmes.note: Compare the capital service lines published within the health allocation. This annual capital provision is not the completed value or lifetime cost of a named hospital project.

programmes.name: Health grants
programmes.note: These are the grant lines explicitly itemised in the health source. They are a subset of the wider health budget, not all grants or purchased services across the HSE.

programmes.name: Other health services
programmes.note: Explore the services placed in this specific source grouping. It is distinct from the separate “Other HSE Services” programme and should not be merged simply because the labels sound similar.

sectors.name: Housing and local government
sectors.tagline: Housing, water, planning and local services
sectors.intro: Explore the housing sector’s published allocation, including the housing department, Uisce Éireann, Tailte Éireann and the Electoral Commission. The sector is wider than building or subsidising homes.
sectors.note: Uisce Éireann appears as a separate 2026 line. A zero in an earlier source category is not evidence that water services had no funding then. Departmental transfers can change the shape of the series.

sectors.name: Education
sectors.tagline: School salaries, supports, pensions and buildings
sectors.intro: See how the first, second and early-years education allocation divides between teaching salaries, special needs assistants, school transport, grants and infrastructure. Higher education sits in a separate sector grouping.
sectors.note: The source has one top-level school programme, so this page opens its detailed lines directly rather than making you visit a duplicate page. School meals are in Social Protection; further and higher education is under Additional Departments.

sectors.name: Transport
sectors.tagline: Public transport, roads, active travel and safety
sectors.intro: Explore public transport, road networks, active travel, aviation and maritime spending. Programme detail distinguishes published operating, administrative and investment lines where the source provides them.
sectors.note: An annual allocation is not the lifetime cost of a railway, road or other capital project. Construction schedules, delivery outputs and multi-year contracts require separate evidence.

sectors.note: For several bodies the official drill-down repeats the full body total as one line. Those are shown as single allocations, not artificially split into staffing, vehicles or individual services.

sectors.name: Debt, EU and other non-voted spending
sectors.tagline: Debt service, EU contributions and other central items
sectors.intro: Separate the service of national debt, the EU Budget contribution and other non-voted expenditure. The sector total is not a measure of the size of Ireland’s national debt.
sectors.note: These are annual spending flows, not the outstanding debt stock. Other non-voted expenditure is a separate source category and must not all be described as debt interest. Non-voted spending is not assigned a current/capital split in this source.

sectors.name: Additional departments
sectors.tagline: Agriculture, disability, enterprise, defence and more
sectors.intro: Open the departments grouped outside the seven other headline sectors. This includes children and disability, further and higher education, agriculture, defence, climate, culture and public administration.
sectors.note: “Additional departments” is a grouping, not a separate administrative agency or a measure of overhead. Each department below has its own published programme breakdown.

programmes.name: Taoiseach’s department group
programmes.note: This source group includes several offices and bodies as well as the Department of the Taoiseach. It is not simply the cost of the Taoiseach’s personal office.
